name: Gain Control
description: Modulation of neural response amplitude by context, attention, or learning. Allows neurons to adapt their responsiveness based on input statistics or task demands. Linked to both bottom-up adaptation and top-down attentional modulation.
computational_signature: gain = f(context, attention, adaptation) where output = gain * input
key_references: Reynolds, J. H., & Heeger, D. J. (2009). The normalization model of attention. Neuron, 61(2), 168-185.
Kohn, A., & Movshon, J. A. (2003). Neuronal adaptation to visual motion in area MT of the macaque. Neuron, 39(3), 465-477.
empirical_evidence: Observed across visual, auditory, and somatosensory cortex. Gain modulation correlates with attention, adaptation state, and behavioral performance. Biophysical mechanisms include neuromodulation (e.g., acetylcholine), shunting inhibition, and input-dependent plasticity.

parameters.time_constant: 100 ms to minutes depending on source
